You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hotspot Sniper｜2026.09.24  Main theme: 10-year yield hits a 2007 high｜Trump-Xi AI contest · Agentic commerce standoff · Memory shorts · Quantum error correction

TEXT:
1. Hot PMI plus a weak auction send the 10-year to 5.11%
September S&P Global composite PMI flash rose to 58.4 from 56.0, a more-than-five-year high, with input prices also firm. Weak demand at the 5-year Treasury auction pushed the 10-year yield to about 5.11%, the highest since 2007; the 2-year hit its highest since 2024. CME FedWatch priced an October hike at roughly 68%–71%. Fed Governor Barr said inflation remains above target and further policy adjustments may be needed. The Dow closed -0.68%, S&P -0.75%, Nasdaq -1.13%.
🎯 Beneficiaries: XLE ( oil rebound, relative), XLF (watch), TLT (inverse); Key catalyst: Rate pricing is driving the indexes; next data and oil will decide whether hike odds keep rising.
2. Trump-Xi Washington visit opens; trade truce extended to Jan. 10
Treasury Secretary Bessent said the U.S. and China arranged to extend the trade truce through Jan. 10, 2027. Xi arrived for a three-day visit; today’s White House ceremony and state dinner include Jensen Huang, Tim Cook, Elon Musk and Sam Altman. Agenda items: the rare-earth export pause, an AI-regulation dialogue, and arms sales to Taiwan. A comprehensive AI pact remains distant. Nvidia fell 1.5% after a winning streak, with forward P/E compressed near ~17x.
🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA , AAPL , TSM ; Key catalyst: Summit language on chip export controls and rare-earth supply — price the joint statement, not the ceremony.
3. Muse hits an e-commerce wall: Amazon blocks, Shopify plugs in
Amazon blocked Meta ’s Muse from shopping on its site, citing unauthorized access, lack of agent identification and credential risk. Shopify, in the same window, said it is partnering deeply with Muse so agent checkouts settle via Shop Pay and generate payment-rail fees. GOOGL fell 3.8%, AMZN 2.2%; META closed higher against the tape; SHOP , which had jumped on the partnership, gave some of it back with the tape. Who owns agent distribution and checkout fees is now a live weekly test.
🎯 Beneficiaries: META, SHOP, AMZN; Key catalyst: Platform open/block policy toward third-party agents, which reallocates traffic and take rates.
4. Memory narrative splits: Burry adds MU shorts, Acer flags supply catch-up
Michael Burry wrote on Substack that he added to shorts in MU, NBIS , PLTR and SOXX “in some size,” citing Acer CEO Jason Chen: some high-end SKUs remain tight, but DDR4 already has “more sellers than buyers,” and mainland capacity will make a multi-year shortage hard to sustain. Memory faded after the early-week rip: MU about -2.2%, SNDK about -3.7%; SOX ended a six-day win streak, -1.23%.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MU, SNDK, SOXX; Key catalyst: Shortage trade versus incoming supply — near-term, whether short commentary and volume unwind the memory premium independently of rates.
5. AI-safety bid lifts cybersecurity: PANW and CRWD up ~5%
While indexes and chips sold off, Palo Alto and CrowdStrike each rose about 5%, PLTR about 3.7%. Flows treated “AI safety / agent-risk defense” as a tradeable sleeve against rate-driven multiple compression in growth. Travel went the other way: ABNB and EXPE dropped more than 7%.
🎯 Beneficiaries: PANW, CRWD, PLTR; Key catalyst: AI-security budget and order validation — watch whether relative strength holds through the rates shock.
6. IonQ ships a real-time error-correction decoder and plugs into Nvidia’s quantum lab
IonQ said it built what it calls the industry’s first end-to-end real-time quantum error-correction decoder that runs on a single commodity CPU, simulating up to 408 logical qubits and 31.5 million-plus operations with ~0.02% stretch under standard noise. It also said Superion 256 will be installed at Nvidia’s accelerated quantum research center to run alongside GPU clusters. IONQ was up more than 10% premarket and closed about +4.4%; RGTI , QBTS and other quantum names followed.
🎯 Beneficiaries: IONQ, NVDA, RGTI; Key catalyst: Error-correction engineering plus the Nvidia hookup — event-driven; require volume confirmation, do not linearly extrapolate commercialization.
Trading note: Rates and oil are driving beta. The tape has rotated from “all-AI” into agent platforms, memory longs vs. shorts, and cyber/quantum sleeves. Today watch Trump-Xi language, new-home sales, and COST after the close. Size with VIX and Treasury volatility.
U.S. equities have been more volatile recently. This is for information only and is not investment advice.
